subject: crab
pitch: A feisty red rock crab with one oversized claw raised in challenge. A wide, knobbly shell in brick red speckled with orange and cream, eyes on stalks, eight jointed walking legs with pointed tips, and claws with dark tips and little teeth on the pinchers. A tiny barnacle and a strand of seaweed cling to the back of its shell.
reasoning:
I'm planning the crab's design facing forward, using a flattened sphere scaled non-uniformly to form the shell shape.

Now I'm thinking about shell texture — small bump spheres plus painted spots in orange/cream for a mottled carapace look. I'm sizing the crab realistically at roughly 40cm wide, setting a root "body" joint and eye-stalk joints, then planning eight legs as chains with hip/knee/tip points per side.

I'm defining the leg geometry: hip, knee, and tip positions spaced along the body sides so the legs splay outward and down to touch the floor, then sweeping tapered tube rods along each chain with pointed tips. For the signature oversized claw, I'm picking the left side to raise it in a challenge pose and starting a separate "arm" chain for it.

I'm building the claw as shoulder-elbow-wrist joints with upper and lower pincer fingers branching off the wrist, using tapered rod sweeps for each finger, small dark spikes as teeth along the inner edges, and a darker cone tip to cap the pincers.

For the eyes, I'll add stalk joints at the body's top-front position, attach pale sphere parts for the eyeball directly to each joint, and offset a darker pupil sphere slightly forward using the joint's local coordinate transform.

For the shell, I'm sizing and positioning an ellipsoid-scaled sphere as the carapace, tuning its radius and y-offset so it sits naturally above the legs with a crab-appropriate width, then scattering small bump spheres across the shell surface using angular placement to give it a knobbly rock-crab texture.

I'm giving the shell a mottled rust-and-cream spot pattern, adding a flattened cream-colored underside sphere for the belly, and placing a tiny barnacle bump on the back, then starting a swept seaweed strand using a wavy catmull-rom path with green coloring trailing off the shell.

Now I'm setting up the leg rig: planning unique joint names that satisfy the naming regex, defining each leg as a chain parented explicitly to the body with role "leg" and named segments, then looping over both sides and four leg positions to compute hip placement along the body's z-axis for a backward-angled crab stance.

I'm working out knee and tip coordinates for each leg path, then sweeping tapered tubes with a rounded start and pointed tip to form the limb shape, letting the chain's joints drive smooth bending. I'm skipping extra knee blobs since the sweep already looks smooth, and moving on to define the claw arm next.

Now I'm setting up the raised claw arm as a chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist, naming the joints so the sweep can taper the arm's radius, then placing a palm sphere at the wrist and starting to build the pincer joints extending forward from it.

Each pincer finger needs a base joint and a tip position so a tapered rod can bridge them, and I need to make sure the `bone` option explicitly binds each rod to its correct joint rather than letting it auto-attach to the nearest point.

I'm sketching coordinates for the upper and lower pincer tips, opening a slight gap between them for a raised pose, and planning dark tapered tip rods plus small spike cones for teeth along the inner edges.

Setting up eye stalks and eyeballs...

Adding dark pupil, mirroring eye stalks for the right side, then setting up the body joint as root for shell parts and planning knob placement on the shell's top surface.

Computing the barnacle's position on the back side of the shell, placing it toward -Z near the top, with a small sphere radius for its size.

I'm sketching a seaweed frond as a swept catmull path curving up and back from near the barnacle base, tapering the sweep radius from thicker at the base to thinner at the tip, colored in a muted green, and binding it to the body bone.

Then I'm adding slab-based leaf shapes near the seaweed with their own point sets and thin thickness for flat foliage. For the mouth, I'm placing a flattened, scaled sphere in a cream-dark tone under the front of the shell, and considering a few small spike shapes along the front edge of the shell as simple teeth or spines, positioned using angular offsets on the ellipsoid surface.

Now I'm defining a helper function that computes points on the shell's ellipsoid surface given angles, so I can consistently place spikes and other features relative to the shell's curvature, then setting up the main shell geometry as a scaled sphere positioned and painted onto the body.

I'm applying a mottled turtle-shell pattern with warm brick-red, orange, and cream tones using spotted texture, and considering whether to add a flattened belly piece beneath the shell for extra realism, though it may end up mostly hidden. Now I'm working out the leg placement logic, looping through each side and leg index to calculate hip, knee, and foot positions that taper and shift backward for the rear legs.

Writing leg chain and sweep code...

Now I'm working out the claw arm: a chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist with a tapered sweep, then a palm sphere, and pincer joints with rods forming the upper and lower pinch tips, positioning everything so the claw reaches forward from the body.

Still refining pincer geometry...

Now I'm working through eye stalks and pupils attached to the body joints, positioning them along the shell's front-top so they sit just outside the carapace surface. I'm also planning the mouth, front spines, barnacle, and seaweed sweep geometry, computing surface points on the shell ellipsoid and building catmull paths for organic curves with tapering radius functions.

I'm also laying out the joint hierarchy—body, eyes, legs, arm, palm, and pincher joints—making sure parent references and chain naming stay consistent, and planning the final module structure with helper vector math, color constants, and the exported builder function that assembles all these parts into the crab model.

I'm designing the claw mechanism now, placing upper and lower pincher joints just inside the palm sphere, then building the pincher fingers as tapered rods with color bands so the tips naturally shift to a darker tone without needing a separate overlapping piece. I'm adding small spike-based teeth along the inner edge of each finger, computing their base position relative to the finger's radius at a given point along its length so they sit flush against the surface and angle slightly forward.

I'm finishing the eye joints and eyeball placement with pupils offset forward, adding the mouth as a flattened sphere, and double-checking that all chain and joint names follow the expected naming conventions so the rig binds correctly.
